title: The levels from Ein Sof to Asiya as one will, and the kelipos that hide it
overview: Chapter 53 is a summary. It goes back over the levels of the chain of descent, from the simple will in the essence of Ein Sof to the last will that makes Asiya, and asks the reader to see them as one act of G-d's choice. The first will is the will of Malchus of Ein Sof; the last is the will of Malchus of Asiya, and between them there are no real differences in levels. The house mashal shows the stages of planning, and the mashal of the wanting shows how one desire runs through many stages at once. The Ofanim are the spiritual source of the four elements and of the cycles of the physical world, and the mazalos channel what happens here; the galgalim revolve because their soul sings praise. The second class turns to the kelipos. The 48 letters of Elokim belong to the people of Cham, who see nature as set apart from G-d. Bilam knew G-d's mind and still had to say he could not go beyond G-d's word; Pharaoh is the separate self-made man. Even the most separate are sometimes humbled, and the Nogah of Asiya is in bittul to G-d.

terms.gloss: contemplation: thinking through the chain of descent until G-d's will is seen in each detail
the general encompassing light, the upper light before the tzimtzum and the lower light after it; the heavens of the verse
the outer vessels of Malchus: the level of the galgalim and the mazalos
the spiritual souls of the planets and the cycles of the physical world
the constellations and the physical channels that influence what happens here
a kli where things are revealed in their essential state; each world has seven
the innermost chamber of a world, where its Keser and its Zeir-Nukva union are revealed
particular providence: G-d's wisdom and will in every detail of the worlds
the level of Asiya that seeks its own pleasure: mostly bad and a little good; kelipas Nogah is its covering
the people of Cham: the 48 last combinations of Elokim, who see nature as set apart from G-d

sections.title: One will in the essence runs through every level
sections.summary: The class sums up the chain of descent: every level, from the simple will in the essence of Ein Sof down to the will that makes Asiya, is one act of G-d's choice.

phrases.he: (נג)
ואחר כל הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: after everything we've explained until now

phrases.he: יובן למשכיל
phrases.en: Based on everything we've explained, it can be understood to someone that studies these things

phrases.he: כללות כל ההתבוננות, מרצון הפשוט העצמי שבעצמות אור אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: the general *hisbonenus*, how we can think about the whole process of the *seder hishtalshelus* beginning from the simple desire in the essence of the infinite light

phrases.he: מחמת בחינת חפץ חסד העצמי שעלה ברצונו הפשוט כו'
phrases.en: which was what caused this desire for kindness, this essential desire for kindness, for desire for kindness that arose in His simple will

phrases.he: (כנזכר לעיל באות יו"ד),
phrases.en: like we talked about in chapter 10

phrases.he: עד בחינת הרצון היותר אחרון, שהוא בחינת הרצון להתהוות עולם העשיה
phrases.en: how that comes down through this whole process until it becomes the desire for everything going on in the physical world of action

phrases.he: בכלל ובפרט,
phrases.en: in general, and more specifically, how it is in every little detail

phrases.he: שנקרא כתר ועתיק יומין דעשיה,
phrases.en: which this desire is called the crown, the desire, and *Atik Yomin*, the inner like pleasure of the world of *Asiya*

phrases.he: והוא מה שכתוב כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה עשה
phrases.en: and this is what it says in the verse, whatever G-d desired He did

blocks.text: A summary: a yichud of all the levels, from the top down through Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya. The next chapter is about the kelipos.
blocks.outOfPlace: The opening of the class, before line 1 is read (read at 0:23): the chapter's summary.

blocks.text: The general contemplation goes this way: the whole chain of descent begins in the simple will of the essence of *Ein Sof*, the desire for kindness that arose in that will, and it runs down to the last will, the will to create the world of *Asiya* in general and in detail. That will is the *Keser* and *Atik Yomin* of *Asiya*, and it is what the verse means: whatever G-d desired, He did. So everything in our physical world is based on G-d's choice.

phrases.he: דודאי כמו שעלה ברצונו להיות חפץ ורצון להאציל,
phrases.en: as it arose in His simple will, to be desire and will to emanate, that first He had the desire to make *Atzilus*, to make the *sefiros*, make G-dliness a certain way

phrases.he: כך עלה חפץ ורצון זה לברוא,
phrases.en: and so that same desire then became the desire to create

phrases.he: וחפץ ורצון ליצר,
phrases.en: and the desire to form

phrases.he: וחפץ ורצון לעשות, הכל
phrases.en: and then the desire to make everything

phrases.he: היה כלול בעצם רצונו הפשוט שבעצמותו
phrases.en: All of these details were already included in that original essential desire in G-d's essence

blocks.text: The first will, to emanate the *sefiros*, became the will to create, to form and to make everything; all of it was in the simple will of His essence.

Go back to the *ratzon kadum* and its stages. A person who builds a house first plans what he wants and talks through his desires. He turns that into a concept of the parts the house will have, designs the exact dimensions and materials, and then builds it. So too the *sefiros* come out in stages: the emanation is the idea of how G-dliness will be revealed in the world. *Beriya* is the idea of Torah, mitzvos and the *neshamos*; *Yetzira* is the idea of the angels and of the systems of nature and human psychology; *Asiya* is what actually happens, as we experience it through our perceptions.
blocks.title: Planning a house

blocks.text: Every detail was already included in that essential desire, so everything expresses Him: it reveals His choice and His taste. Each thing is part of the general desire and has its own flavor, expressing something nothing else does.

phrases.he: על דרך משל אדם שעלה ברצונו העצמי להיות לו רצון לאיזה ענין דבר מה,
phrases.en: for example, with a metaphor of a person, when a person wants something

phrases.he: שאף על פי שבפרט הרי מיד הוא בא בחילוקי רצונות ממדריגה למדריגה,
phrases.en: even though there's all these stages

phrases.he: עד בחינת הרצון היותר אחרון שהוא בחינת רצון לסוף מעשה ממש,
מכל מקום הכל עלה בבת אחת בעצם רצונו כו',
מבלי חילוק מדריגות כלל
phrases.en: without really thinking about all those separate stages

blocks.text: Take a person who wants something. Even though the will goes through many stages, every day it is obvious that a person plugs his essence straight into what he is doing and says, in effect, this is what I want. A child who wants an ice cream cone, or someone who wants a guitar, does not think through the stages; the wanting is one act.
blocks.title: Wanting an ice cream cone

blocks.text: To see the stages, ask why the child wants the cone. The essential desire to live and to experience G-dliness comes from the *neshama*; it is translated into *Adam Kadmon*, the self-image and world view. The child associates the cone with good memories and sweetness, and through that process he decides he wants it.
blocks.title: Wanting an ice cream cone

blocks.text: A person traveled to a place where diamonds were everywhere, expecting to get rich. There the currency was chicken fat. He forgot the diamonds, became a tycoon in chicken fat, and shipped it home, where it all rotted. All he had left were a few small diamonds he had never noticed in his cuff. You can easily break any of those stages.
blocks.title: The diamonds and the chicken fat

blocks.text: Money is only paper, a number in a bank account. It means something because it buys what helps you fulfill your purpose and mission, and that ends in the essential desire, which is a G-dly thing.
blocks.title: Money is paper

blocks.text: Even with the whole process, the will arose all at once in His essence. A regular person who has his connections set up says, "I want that," without thinking of the stages; the connections function as one unit.

The Rebbe says in many sichos it is fine to daven for physical needs, when they are plugged into the whole: one wants them to serve G-d and do one's mission. Some Kabbalah sources, the Baal Shem Tov and the Maggid say daven only for the Shechina.

The same with a physical mitzvah: the desire may be clothed in a physical *levush* (garment). One does it because the *Shulchan Aruch* says so, though that rests on a *machlokes* in the Gemara, and he need not know that. He knows the rabbi said this is what G-d wants, so he wants it, and it plugs into the whole.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב באות ז',
phrases.en: like we talked about in chapter seven

phrases.he: שאין חילוקי מדריגות בבחינת הכתרים דאבי"ע,
אף על פי שבהשתלשלות
phrases.en: that even though there's all these stages

phrases.he: מבחינת מלכות שבעליון נעשה כתר לתחתון כו')
phrases.en: but really when it comes to the *ratzon*, it's really just one *ratzon*, and there's not a real *hishtalshelus* in the *Kesarim*

blocks.text: As chapter seven teaches, the crowns of Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya have no differences in levels. The descent makes Malchus above a crown below, but there is one will, going directly from the person to the thing he wants.

phrases.he: כך לגבי עצמות רצונו הפשוט שבבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: And so too when it comes to G-d's will

phrases.he: אין חילוק מדריגות בין חפץ ורצון להאציל, בין חפץ ורצון לעשות
כו'

blocks.text: The same holds for the simple will in Ein Sof's essence: no difference in levels between the desire to emanate and the desire to act. Once G-d chooses, the choice expresses His will. He could have chosen otherwise, but then the whole chain would have to change.
The Rebbe has a whole sicha on Yehoshua stopping the sun at the battle of Givon: everything the chain of descent required for that happened. It all works as one unit.
blocks.title: Yehoshua stops the sun

sections.title: The first and last will: from Ein Sof to the lowest world
sections.summary: Ani rishon and ani acharon mark the two ends of the will, and the Ofanim are the spiritual source of the elements and of the cycles of the physical world, and the mazalos are their channels.

phrases.he: וזהו אני ראשון,
phrases.en: and this is what it says, I am first and I am last

phrases.he: ברצון שבמלכות דאין סוף, מקור הרצון להאציל,
phrases.en: I am first, the will in *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*, the source of the will for *Atzilus*

phrases.he: ואני אחרון, ברצון האחרון שבמלכות דעשיה להתהוות עולם השפל היותר
phrases.en: that is the same as *I am last*, the final *Malchus*, the last will in the *Malchus* of *Asiya*, to create this final physical world

phrases.he: אחרון, שהן האופנים והמזלות,
phrases.en: which these details of the physical world are the *Ofanim*, the angels

phrases.he: שהמה שרשי התהוות רוחניות הד' יסודות דאש רוח מים ועפר
phrases.en: and those are the spiritual source for the creation of the physical elements of fire, wind, water, and earth

phrases.he: ורוחניות דומם צומח חי הגשמיים
phrases.en: and the spiritual souls of the *domem*, *tzomeach*, *chai*, the inanimate, plant, and animal things

blocks.text: *Ani rishon* is the will in *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*, the source of the will to emanate. *Ani acharon* is the last will, in the *Malchus* of *Asiya*, to create the lowest world.
Just as He chose the ten *sefiros* and how they will be, G-d is also choosing the weather today, how trees and squirrels work, and everything that plays out in my life today.

The *Ofanim* are the spiritual soul inside the planets, the weather and the cycles that control the physical world. The *mazalos* are the physical channels, like the sun and the stars, that affect what happens here. It seems G-d set up a machine called nature, but He controls it, and His choice comes through all of it.

The *Ofanim* are the spiritual source of the four elements and of the spiritual souls of the inanimate, plant and animal, and everything physical comes through these *malachim*, as the end of *Etz Chaim* explains.
Yes. Cycles are built into us to keep us balanced and alive, what they call homeostasis, and they come from the *Ofanim*.
blocks.question: Just as the weather always changes, does our mood always change too?

blocks.text: Sleep and waking, blood sugar, and all the body's cycles come from the *Ofanim*.
When these forces get out of whack they cause illness. A hungry, thirsty or tired person has a different mood and cannot concentrate. Life, too, goes through cycles of growing and maturing.

There are layers of complexity, from the basic physics of the world down to chemistry and biology. *Etz Chaim* goes through how these levels make up *nefesh*, *ruach*, *neshama*, *chaya* and *yechida* in everything, with the *kelipa* on top of them.
G-d makes His choices, which change things, and we make ours, which also change things; the Arizal discusses this relation elsewhere.
A modern analogy, I think, is a website or video game: the designer sets it up to work a certain way, a click triggers code, and it is designed for the user to interact with and change things.
blocks.title: The designer and the video game

blocks.text: We have limited control over what we can change, but within that we are given the ability to choose and change things, and that ability is itself part of G-d's will.

A person does not really know how to move his hand. G-d has to make all the cells, nerves, biology, chemistry and physics work. G-d gives him a consciousness that pushes a button, "I want to move my hand," and G-d does the rest. Once it is set up, a person just says, "I wanted to do that."
blocks.title: Moving my hand

blocks.text: When a person commits a crime, we say he did it, even though one could say the hand is just atoms and biology. It is all connected. If someone breaks a window with a baseball bat, or throws a ball through it, even though they let go, we say their will was clothed in the thing, and they did it: they had the intention and the energy.
blocks.title: The window

blocks.text: So we should look around, even if we study the science, and recognize that all these things are there. First is our perception, the world of Asiya; then the objective world, Yetzira; then the inner, G-dly level of how our souls work and our purpose in Torah and mitzvos. Behind that are the G-dly aspects of the sefiros. All of it is designed by G-d's choice.
He comes back to line 5: no difference in levels in the simple will of the essence, and the last will, clothed in Asiya, is the same will as the first.
blocks.outOfPlace: A recap of lines 5 and 6, given after the discussion of the cycles and the mashalim and before line 7 is read (at 17:38).

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב בסוף העץ חיים) שזהו
נכלל הכל במה שכתוב כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה בעצמות עשה,
phrases.en: All this is included in what it says, that everything G-d desired He did

phrases.he: שכולל כל ההשתלשלות דקו, עד סוף עולם העשיה,
phrases.en: And that one little verse is the *hisbonenus* to recognize that G-d's will is coming through everything from the beginning of the *seder hishtalshelus*, through the *kav*, all the way down to the end of the world of *Asiya*

phrases.he: דהיינו שכוללם יחד
phrases.en: that He includes all of them together

blocks.text: The whole verse, "whatever G-d desired in His essence, He did," includes the whole chain of descent from the kav down to the end of Asiya. It is the hisbonenus showing G-d's will coming through all of it, including all of them together.

phrases.he: שנקרא הכל בבחינת עשיה לבד,
phrases.en: that it's that whole process of the whole *seder hishtalshelus* all the way down to the final action is all just called G-d doing it

phrases.he: כי שרש האצילות ושרש העשיה שוין ממש לגבי עצמותו כו'
phrases.en: because the source of *Atzilus* and the source of *Asiya* are completely equal to G-d

blocks.text: Even though there is a whole process, it is all just called G-d acting. It is like a phone call that goes through satellites and computers, and we just say, "I am talking to you," because it is all connected. Our soul works through the brain and physiology until it comes out as our choice expressed in what we do.
blocks.title: The phone call

blocks.text: We want to see how the parts fit together: look what G-d did, how He set it up. The source of Atzilus and the source of Asiya are completely equal to G-d.
G-d decides how He wants it, a direct expression of His essence. At every level, you can very quickly get to the point of asking, "Why is it like that?"
Just because G-d wants it that way, on every level. There did not have to be ten *sefiros*; there could have been twelve. He chose these ten, in this order, and that is His choice.

The same is true on the level of action. A person did not have to be born to these parents or at this time; his nose and the weather today could have been different. Every little detail is G-d's choice.

phrases.he: וזהו עשה
phrases.en: and this is what it says that He did

phrases.he: בשמים, סובב הכללי דטהירו עילאה, וטהירו תתאה
phrases.en: in the heavens, which means both the general surrounding light of the upper light before the *tzimtzum* and the lower light after the *tzimtzum*, which is the *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: וארץ דבחינת ממלא כל עלמין כו',
phrases.en: and on the earth, in the light that comes into everything individually

phrases.he: הכל בהשוואה אחת
phrases.en: it's all equal

blocks.text: *Heavens* is the general encompassing light of the upper and lower light, the *ratzon kadum*; *earth* is the light that fills every creature individually. There is a general plan that is the same for everything, and G-d made each creature unique, with its own role. It is all equal: an expression of His will and His choice.

sections.title: Adam Kadmon and the particular way: seeing G-d's hand in each detail
sections.summary: Adam Kadmon's head and feet are the same to G-d, and the aim of every contemplation is to see G-d's simple will in each detail, down to the last one.

phrases.he: (כידוע דעקב דאדם קדמון שמסתיים בסוף העשיה וראשו במחשבה כללית בתחלת הקו,
phrases.en: as is known, *Adam Kadmon*, which is this general *partzuf* or general world that extends to the whole, encompasses the whole chain of descent, its feet go all the way down to the world of action, but its head is all the way up in the general thought that's the beginning of the *kav*

phrases.he: (וכמו באדם הראשון, שאמרו שקודם החטא היה רגליו בעשיה וראשו בבריאה
phrases.en: And this is what it says about *Adam HaRishon*, that before he sinned his feet were in the world of *Asiya* and his head was in the world of *Beriya*

phrases.he: (נקרא אדם דבריאה יש מאין כו')
phrases.en: that's like we said, *Adam Kadmon* is called the man of *Beriya*, *yesh me'ayin*, but it extends all the way down

blocks.text: As is known, *Adam Kadmon*, whose feet reach down to the end of *Asiya* and whose head is in the general thought at the start of the *kav*, encompasses the whole chain of descent. The first man was the same: before he sinned, his feet were in *Asiya* and his head in *Beriya*. *Adam Kadmon* is called the man of *Beriya*, *yesh me'ayin*, but its encompassing extends all the way down.
blocks.title: Adam Kadmon's feet and head

phrases.he: (והיינו וכל קומה לפניך תשתחוה כו'
phrases.en: and this is what it says, that every posture bows down to You

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)
phrases.en: as is explained elsewhere

blocks.text: Every posture bows down to You, even Adam Kadmon's whole posture. The head and feet are the same to G-d; as He creates the beginning, He creates the end, all revealing His will. The system does not limit G-d's choice at all; it is just how He set it up, as is explained elsewhere.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר המכוון בכל ההתבוננות,
phrases.en: and this is the main purpose, the main intention, the main goal or aim in any *hisbonenus* that we're doing

phrases.he: בכל פרט ופרט שבכל ההשתלשלות דקו, מלפני הצמצום הראשון עד סוף העשיה,
phrases.en: when we're learning and thinking about all the details of the whole chain of descent, from before the *tzimtzum* all the way down to the end of the world of action

phrases.he: רק להיות נכלל הכל באחדות הפשוטה,
phrases.en: the whole thing of learning about all this stuff is to, in a way, get it out of the way, to see how it's all connected to G-d's simple unity

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת עצמות אור אין סוף עד שיקבע בנפש
phrases.en: which is the essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, until it becomes very firmly implanted in a person

phrases.he: גם בסדר השגחה אלהי״ת בפרטיות, עד הפרט היותר אחרון

blocks.text: The aim of any *hisbonenus*, in every detail from before the first *tzimtzum* to the end of *Asiya*, is to see it all included in the simple unity of *Or Ein Sof*.
We learn all this to get it out of the way: to see it connected to G-d's simple unity, until awareness of G-d and His particular providence is firmly fixed in the soul.

It is not enough to believe that G-d exists in general. See G-d choosing every detail, and see *hashgacha pratis* as His wisdom and will in every detail of the worlds, in Torah and mitzvos, down to the last detail.

phrases.he: שהוא גם בעולם הגלגלים והמזלות,
phrases.en: even the world of the *galgalim* means like the stars and the planets, and the different constellations

phrases.he: שהם רק מט' כלים החיצונים דמלכות דמלכות דעשיה,
phrases.en: the external vessels of *Malchus de-Malchus* of *Asiya*

phrases.he: שהוא רק על פי רצונו הפשוט שבעצמות אור אין סוף ממש
phrases.en: and all of this is just based on Hashem's simple *ratzon* in the essence of the infinite

blocks.text: The *galgalim* and the *mazalos* are the outer vessels of *Malchus de-Malchus* of *Asiya*. That level looks separate, like the *reshimu*, as if thrown: G-d made our world look thrown, and He set the stars and planets in motion so that they seem to go on their own.

They keep orbiting on their own, the level of Malchus de-Malchus of Asiya, but they are tools that influence the sun, the moon, the weather and the tides: physical channels for what happens. All of it rests on Hashem's simple will in the essence of Or Ein Sof.

phrases.he: וכמו שאנו אומרים, ומסדר את הכוכבים במשמרותיהם ברקיע כרצונו דוקא,
phrases.en: like we say, that G-d arranges the stars in their posts in the heavens according to His will

phrases.he: דהיינו כרצונו הפשוט שבעצמותו ממש
phrases.en: it is because that's what G-d decided should be

phrases.he: מטעם הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: from His very essence, for the reason explained

blocks.text: As we say, G-d arranges the stars in their posts in the raki'a, precisely according to His will.

Every star and planet is set exactly where it will be. According to modern cosmology, people like to think of the Big Bang as against Torah, but he thinks it is the opposite: it is not an accident or a disconnect from G-d. The *midrashim* say the world started small, like a mustard seed, and G-d expanded it out. People once opposed the idea, insisting the world always was as it is, because they did not want a beginning and a creation.

Whatever the right theory, G-d arranged it and put it in place. It did not have to be this way. Earth is uniquely positioned: a little closer or farther from the sun, or without Jupiter clearing the asteroids, we would be hit every other day.

Every constant of physics is fine-tuned to exact values so that we can live. One of the big problems in science is that they do not understand why the values are what they are. It is because that is what G-d decided.

sensitivity.reason: A criticism of scientists as a group: that science does not understand, and has no answer, to why the constants are what they are. The point is his view of how science thinks, so it is raw.
sensitivity.publishable: Every constant of physics is fine-tuned to exact values so that we can live. One of the big open questions in science is why the values are what they are. It is because that is what G-d decided.

blocks.text: The point is to see through the illusion of nature. Those are tools G-d set up; He chooses how they go, and He controls them. That is an expression of His will in His very essence.

phrases.he: ופירוש במשמרותיהם,
phrases.en: what does it mean that He set them in their posts

phrases.he: היינו גם בבחינת היכלות דקליפת נוגה דעשיה,
phrases.en: This means even in the chambers of *kelipas Nogah* of the physical world

phrases.he: שהמזלות הקבועים ברקיע,
phrases.en: that G-d set up the actual stars and planets and constellations in the physical sky

phrases.he: היינו בבחינת נוגה דעשיה
phrases.en: This is in the level of *Nogah* of *Asiya*

blocks.text: "In their posts" means that the fixed stars in the *raki'a* are in the chambers of *kelipas Nogah* of *Asiya*. G-d set up the actual stars, planets and constellations of the physical sky, in the level of *Nogah* of *Asiya*.

sections.title: The Kodesh Kodashim: the union of Zeir and Nukva, and why we learn the levels
sections.summary: Asiya's Kodesh Kodashim is where Zeir Anpin and Nukva unite, the essential joined to the circumstantial; the class then turns to why one must learn these levels.

phrases.he: כי עשר ספירות דעשיה בבחינת אורות וכלים והיכלות כו',
phrases.en: because everything, all the *sefiros* of the world of *Asiya* with their lights and their vessels and the *heichalos*

phrases.he: הכל הוא בבחינת ביטול היש לאין בתכלית,
phrases.en: everything is completely nullified in a way

phrases.he: כידוע
דבהיכל
phrases.en: I'm just going to mention here, what's the idea of a *heichal*

phrases.he: קודש קדשים דעשיה
phrases.en: that in the Holy of Holies of the world of *Asiya*

phrases.he: שם יחוד זעיר אנפין ונוקבא דעשיה,
phrases.en: that's where you have the union of *Zeir* and *Nukva*

phrases.he: כמו בבית המקדש שלמטה כו'
phrases.en: for example, in the physical *Beis HaMikdash* down here

blocks.text: The ten *sefiros* of *Asiya*, with their lights, vessels and *heichalos*, are all nullified to nothing. Nature looks like a system, but nothing dictates how it must be; it is G-d's choice that makes it exactly this way, in exactly the position it is in.

What is a heichal? It is like a person's house or room, where he can be very self-expressive and have everything revealed. A regular kli limits something so it can be condensed and given to someone else; a heichal is a kli where things are revealed more in their essential state.

Each world has seven heichalos, and the Kodesh Kodashim of every world is where Keser Chabad is revealed. In Asiya's Kodesh Kodashim, Zeir Anpin and Nukva unite. Zeir is the way G-d sets things up; Nukva is our perception, and the unchanging G-dly forces as revealed within time and space. G-d combines essential things with external ones: light and a kli, a levush, or the absolute will coming into a composite will.
That is the union of *Zeir* and *Nukva*: the essential joined to the circumstantial. In *Asiya* it is how G-d sets up the world, and the exact *halacha* as it is applied.
The same union is revealed in the *luchos* and the physical *Kodesh Kodashim*, where G-d's will was revealed for people in these circumstances.

The history goes from Avraham to Mitzrayim to the Torah. The spirit of the law is unchanging, for all people, beyond the Torah as it is; that was the whole fight between the angels and the Jews. It could have come out in many ways, which is why there is a *machlokes*: different opinions on how it comes out. Recognize both the spirit of the law and the Torah as it came out.

How it actually came out is also G-d's will: He chose these circumstances, and most people need things a certain way, which is why it is paskened that way. Even though it could have been different, the custom and accepted practice is also His will.

Embrace both: seek the essential things that do not change, and accept what is, which is also G-d's choice. Like the soul and the body: the soul is infinite; the body is limited, but G-d chose this body, a choice even higher than the soul.

Yes, there is a danger of distraction, which *Shaar HaYichud* and Ibn Tibbon's introduction discuss. Still, learn the levels properly, with *yiras Shamayim*; the Frierdiker Rebbe says success in Torah comes from that, not from how smart one is.
blocks.question: Is there a danger in getting lost in the details, learning all these levels, so that it seems we are trying to forget them?
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 16 and the explanation on the Kodesh Kodashim, in the general discussion of how to learn the levels. The student's question and his answer are about the chapter as a whole.

blocks.text: The goal is simplicity. Why learn the levels? Two reasons. We begin with a simple simplicity, like a small child, but we get fooled by the masks of the *kelipos* and by misconceptions, and stop seeing G-dliness. Learning uncovers G-dliness.
blocks.outOfPlace: The general discussion after line 16, on learning the levels; placed with the question on the danger of the details.

blocks.text: Without these tools one cannot fully reveal this essence. A person can do it childlike, but understanding lets him appreciate it deeper. The *Tanya* says learning the *seder hishtalshelus* brings a *lev shalem*, the main thing.
blocks.outOfPlace: The general discussion after line 16, on learning the levels.

blocks.text: Simple faith does not mean not understanding: understand what you can, and what is left to *emuna* is pure. Without learning there is confusion; learning brings clarity, and it is a mitzvah.
blocks.outOfPlace: The general discussion after line 16, on learning the levels.

blocks.text: It is one of the 613 mitzvos: to know G-d, the first mitzvah in the Rambam. Learning this fulfills the mitzvos of loving, fearing and uniting G-d, and the six constant mitzvos; it is the soul of all the mitzvos.
blocks.outOfPlace: The general discussion after line 16, on learning the levels.

sections.title: Everything is nullified: the angels, the chariot, the horse and the rider
sections.summary: The angels and the planets are in complete bittul; even the forces that look evil are G-d's vehicles, as the horse is to its rider and the axe is to the one who wields it.

phrases.he: ונשמות ומלאכים דעשיה הן בתכלית הביטול כמו שכתוב וצבא השמים לך משתחוים,
phrases.en: and also the souls and angels of *Asiya*, they're all completely nullified, like it says that all of the hosts of the heavens bow down to you

phrases.he: וכמו האופנים וחיות דעשיה
phrases.en: like, for example, just the physical angels of the *Ofanim* and the *Chayos*

phrases.he: וגם חומר וכלי האופנים בבחינת הביטול בתכלית,
phrases.en: and even the physical vessel of the *Ofanim*, which is like the *mazalos* and the planets and the sun and these things, they're all completely nullified

phrases.he: וכמובן במרכבת יחזקאל בחיות ואופנים דיצירה
phrases.en: as is understood from the vision of the chariot that's in the *navi*, in the *Chayos* and *Ofanim* of *Yetzira*

phrases.he: וכך גם במרכבה דסוסים שחורים ואדומים דזכריה
phrases.en: even in *Zechariah* he describes, during the time of *galus*, a chariot with these red and black horses

phrases.he: בזמן הגלות, שהמלכות מלובשת בע' שרים דנוגה דעשיה,
phrases.en: when *Malchus* is enclothed, expressed through the seventy *sarim* of *Nogah*

phrases.he: גם הם בתכלית הביטול כסוס לגבי רוכב
phrases.en: they're also totally nullified, they're also a *merkava*

blocks.text: The souls and angels of Asiya are in complete bittul: all the hosts of heaven bow to G-d. So too the physical Ofanim and Chayos, even their vessel: the mazalos and the sun. As in Yechezkel's chariot, the Chayos and Ofanim of Yetzira are nullified too.

In Zechariah's vision of the red and black horses, all the angels are G-d's chariot: wherever He wants to go, they go. In exile, *Malchus* is clothed in the seventy *sarim* of *Nogah* of *Asiya*, expressed through *kelipas Nogah*. They too are completely nullified, and they too are a chariot.

That is the point of Yechezkel's prophecy, and of Zechariah's too. In exile there are forces that seem to come from the kelipa, like Achashverosh and Haman in the Purim story. G-d moves them by His will and decides what will happen; even when they seem evil, they are part of His plan. Like a horse to its rider, the rider decides where it goes.

phrases.he: וכמו הנה יהו״ה רוכב על עב קל כו'
phrases.en: like it says that G-d rides on a thin cloud

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בזהר, כעננים למרכב כו'
phrases.en: like it says in the *Zohar*, like clouds to a rider

phrases.he: ועל דרך שאמר היתפאר הגרזן על החוצב בו כו'
phrases.en: like it says, that will you praise the axe instead of the person that's wielding

blocks.text: G-d rides on a thin cloud, like clouds to a rider, as the *Zohar* says. The *kelipos* seem to hide G-dliness, but He controls them and they do what He wants.
blocks.title: The rider on the cloud

blocks.text: Like the verse: will you praise the axe instead of the one who wields it? You praise the builder, not the tool. Everything is a tool G-d uses, like a craftsman's hammer; as we say on *Rosh Hashana*, everything is in His hands like clay.
blocks.title: The axe and the one who wields it

sections.title: Cham, the Nile and the veils: the 48 letters that hide G-dliness
sections.summary: The 48 letters of the name Elokim are the outer level of the Name; the people of Cham see nature as separate, and G-d hides His hashgacha behind curtains, yet He is King over the nations.

phrases.he: והגם שיש בהם חילוקי מדריגות בהשתלשלות רבות עד אותן שמקבלים על ידי ריבוי מסכים מבחינת אחוריים דאחוריים דאלהי״ם,
phrases.en: even though as we go down through the *seder hishtalshelus* that there are creatures and *malachim* that are receiving only from the most external levels of the name of *Elokim*

phrases.he: ממ"ח צירופים האחרונים
phrases.en: from the 48 last combinations

phrases.he: שנקרא אדמת בני חם,
phrases.en: that's what it says, the people of *Cham*

phrases.he: בתכלית ההסתר והצמצום
phrases.en: where things are completely concealed and completely hidden

phrases.he: בכמה מיני מסכים והבדלות
phrases.en: through many types of curtains and separations

phrases.he: עד שנקרא לבוש שק ועור,
phrases.en: until it's like it's covered in this thick leather, sackcloth or leather garment

phrases.he: כמו אלביש שמים קדרות
phrases.en: like it says in the verse

phrases.he: ושק אשים כסותם
phrases.en: and I will make their garments into sackcloth

phrases.he: כו' כידוע,
phrases.en: in other words, He's going to hide His *hashgacha pratis* and make it look like everything is just running according to nature

phrases.he: וכמו שאמר המבדיל כו'
phrases.en: like it says, that G-d makes these separations

phrases.he: מכל מקום נאמר מלך אלהי״ם על גוים
phrases.en: nevertheless, it says that G-d is the King over the nations of the world

phrases.he: כו'
phrases.en: who would not fear You, the King of the nations

phrases.he: מי לא ייראך מלך הגוים כו' שמלכותו בכל משלה
phrases.en: that G-d rules over everything

blocks.text: The 48 are the combinations that start with the last two letters of *Elokim*, *yud* and *mem*, after the 72 that start with the first three. Following *Sefer Yetzira*, two stones make two houses, three stones make six, and five letters make 120 combinations. The first three letters give 72 combinations and the last two, the *yud* and *mem*, give 48. Those 48 are *Elokim acherim*, the outer aspect of the Name, called *Edomas bnei Cham*.

The 48 are the letters of *Cham*: they receive G-d and nature only externally and see them as separate. In *Egypt*, the Nile was a set system and they did not need rain or G-d. Seeing nature as set in stone is this external aspect.

We live in cities of brick and steel, which creates the illusion that everything is mechanized and insulates us from nature. In the woods reality is more transcendent, and G-dliness is seen more easily. People freak out that the weather is so crazy, but it is simply chaotic, and not a surprise.
blocks.title: The city and the woods

blocks.text: Through many kinds of curtains the natural world and its laws can make a person see everything through thick leather or sackcloth that hides the light, not something sheer that lets it through.

The verse, "I will make the heavens like cauldrons," simply means no rain, but here it is explained as meaning that we do not see where G-dliness comes from. "I will make their garments sackcloth": Hashem hides His hashgacha pratis and makes everything look as if it runs by nature.
The idea appears in *Torah Ohr* and *Likkutei Torah*: curtains separate. In the *Beis HaMikdash* a curtain divided the *Kodesh Kodashim*, and there is also a curtain between holiness and unholiness.

G-d is King over the nations too. Even atheistic nations are forced to acknowledge Him; everything is by His will. No one escapes His dominion, even when it does not seem so, as the Purim story shows.

phrases.he: וראיה
phrases.en: and the proof

phrases.he: מבלעם,
phrases.en: is from Balaam

phrases.he: שהיה מבחינת רע דנוגה,
phrases.en: that he was from the level of *ra* of *Nogah*

phrases.he: בחינת דעת דקליפה
phrases.en: he was from the level of *daas* of *kelipa*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב ויודע דעת עליון כו',
phrases.en: like it says about Balaam, that he knew, so to speak, the mind of G-d, the knowledge of G-d

phrases.he: אמר לא אוכל לעבור את פי יהו״ה לעשות קטנה כו'
phrases.en: nevertheless Balaam had to say, I'm not able to transgress the word of Hashem, to do even the smallest thing, that everything he did had to be according to Hashem's will

blocks.text: The proof is Balaam, from the level of the evil of Nogah and the daas of the kelipa, as it says, "he knew the daas elyon." Moshe is the daas of kedusha, and Balaam, with the daas of the kelipa, opposed him. Still, Balaam had to say, "I cannot transgress the word of Hashem, to do even the smallest thing." Though he wanted to be separate, rich and famous, G-d runs the world and he had to follow it.

sections.title: Bilam's donkey, Pharaoh and the three impure kelipos: separation and the humbling
sections.summary: The donkey stands for a harsh receiver in the kelipos; Pharaoh is the separate self-made man, and even the most separate are sometimes humbled when G-d remembers them.

phrases.he: (וגם מאתונו
phrases.en: we also see that from his donkey

phrases.he: בחינת נוקבא דזעיר אנפין דקליפה, שהיא יותר קשה
phrases.en: which that donkey represents the feminine aspect of *Zeir Anpin* of *kelipa*, which is more harsh

phrases.he: (כמו שיתבאר שבאת זה לעומת זה בחינת הנוקבא יותר קשה מכולם כו')
phrases.en: like it explains elsewhere, that in the realm of the *kelipos*, the feminine aspect is worse, more difficult or more damaging than all of them

phrases.he: כתיב
phrases.en: and it's written

phrases.he: ותט האתון כו'
phrases.en: the donkey, when he saw the angel, had to turn, he turned away, three times from the angel

phrases.he: וגם בלעם אמר אם רע בעיניך אשובה לי כו')
phrases.en: and once Balaam saw the angel, he also said, "If it's bad in your eyes, I'll return"

blocks.text: The donkey is the feminine aspect of *Zeir Anpin* of the *kelipa*, and in the *kelipa* the recipient is harsher: a depression where a person looks to fill a void and receive any pleasure or sensation.
In the realm of the *kelipos* the feminine aspect is harder than all of them. A *ma'amar* explains: *simcha* comes from humility, depression from arrogance, shown in this kind of receiving.
The donkey turned away from the angel three times, and Balaam also said, "If it is bad in Your eyes, I will return." Both showed they were subservient to G-d.

phrases.he: והגם שיש מהם שהן בבחינת יש נפרד גמור לומר כחי ועוצם ידי כו',
phrases.en: even though there are some of these that are completely separate, saying my might and my strength, like Pharaoh who said that it's my might and my strength that made me

phrases.he: כמו שר של מצרים שאמר לי יאורי כו'
phrases.en: and this is the *sar* of Egypt, not just Pharaoh physically, but the whole ethos, the whole mentality

phrases.he: וכמאמר רבותינו זכרונם לברכה יודעים את רבונם ומתכוונין למרוד בו,
phrases.en: like our sages say, they know their Maker and intend to rebel against Him

phrases.he: הנה זהו מבחינת ג' קליפות הטמאות לגמרי,
phrases.en: So this type of perspective of being totally separate from G-d and trying to rebel against their Creator, that's the realm of the three totally impure *kelipos*

phrases.he: וגם הם נכנעים לפרקים
phrases.en: but even they are sometimes forced to be humble and to admit that everything is coming from Hashem

phrases.he: כאשר יפקוד יהו״ה עליהם
phrases.en: when Hashem remembers them and judges them

blocks.text: Some people or nations are completely separate from G-d, saying "my might and my strength," like Pharaoh, who said he made himself.
This is the *sar* of Egypt, the ethos of Egypt: we build our own destiny and put dams on the Nile. Pharaoh's job was to represent taming nature, an unchanging force, which is why he was stubborn.
Such people have an arrogance, not acknowledging what is beyond their control. You have that a little in a lot of Western, American fiction and mythology: we can do anything with our will.

sensitivity.reason: A jab at a country and its popular culture ("Western, American" fiction and mythology), in passing. The point (that people overrate their will) is kept.
sensitivity.publishable: Such people have an arrogance, not acknowledging what is beyond their control. You have that a little in a lot of modern fiction and mythology: we can do anything with our will.

blocks.text: The whole superhero genre is an ego trip: "I can do anything, I will always be right, I could dodge all the bullets." There is some truth to that, but a lot of it expresses feeling totally separate, "I don't need G-d, I don't need anybody's help." Like the *sar* of Egypt, Pharaoh said the Nile is his, and "I made myself."

Like our sages say, these know their Maker and intend to rebel against Him: the realm of the three totally impure kelipos, where the kelipa goes all the way down to a perspective totally separate from G-d.
Even those are sometimes humbled, and even in the realm of *Nogah*, a self-centered person who wants success must follow the reality G-d sets out.
The three impure *kelipos* are willing to be delusional and enter a fantasy to do whatever they want, as Pharaoh did. Even they are sometimes forced to say, "I have to listen."

You had that a little with COVID: in America there was this idea, "I can do whatever I want," until a person is forced to admit it is not that simple: one sneeze can affect millions, and things have real consequences.

sensitivity.reason: A jab at a country ("in America") and its people, in passing. The point (people think they can do whatever they want, and COVID shows otherwise) is kept.
sensitivity.publishable: You had that a little with COVID: there was this idea, "I can do whatever I want," until a person is forced to admit it is not that simple: one sneeze can affect millions, and things have real consequences.

blocks.text: That is when G-d remembers them and judges them: when the leaders of the nations are humbled, the consequences come.

phrases.he: כמבואר בנבואת הנביאים על כמה שרי אומות העולם כו'
phrases.en: like it's explained in the *Nevi'im*, about many of the leaders of the nations of the world, like Nevuchadnezzar and Pharaoh, and all these different things, that there come a certain time when G-d humbles them

blocks.text: As the prophets explain, G-d humbles leaders of nations, such as Nevuchadnezzar and Pharaoh, at a certain time.

sections.title: Nogah and the planets: the song that keeps the spheres turning
sections.summary: The Nogah of Asiya is mostly bad and a little good, and even the planets and constellations are in constant bittul, which is why they revolve: their soul sings the praise.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת נגה, גם בבחינת נגה דעשיה שרובו רע ומיעוטו טוב,
phrases.en: but when we're still in the realm of *Nogah*, which is not like actively seeking to deny G-d, it's just seeking its own pleasure, and it is mostly bad and a little bit good

phrases.he: המה בבחינת ביטול תמיד,
phrases.en: like Balaam, they are constantly *batel* to G-d, because as long as a person is rational

phrases.he: כמו הגלגלים והמזלות שהן ע' שרים
phrases.en: like all the planets and all the constellations and all these things, which are the 70 *malachim* that are in charge of the 70 nations

phrases.he: דכתיב בהם גם כן וצבא השמים לך משתחוים
phrases.en: like it says about them, that even about them it says that the hosts of heaven bow down to you

phrases.he: ואומרים שירה בכל יום כו'
phrases.en: they are forced to follow G-d's rules of how He sets things up, and they sing the praises to G-d every day

blocks.text: The *Nogah* of *Asiya* is mostly bad and a little good: it seeks its own pleasure, but still listens to G-d, like Balaam. Such a person is constantly *batel* to G-d, since a rational person who wants success must follow G-d's rules.
The planets and constellations are the seventy *malachim* in charge of the seventy nations, and about them too the verse says the hosts of heaven bow down to You.

They are forced to follow G-d's rules and sing praise every day, so their behavior shows they are controlled by something beyond them. Like the weather: the laws of nature are set, yet there is a chaos beyond our understanding, which is just how G-d decides.

phrases.he: וכידוע בענין הטעם לסיבוב התמידי דחומר הגלגלים,
phrases.en: like it's explained about the reason that the planets and the stars and everything are constantly revolving, why are they constantly orbiting

phrases.he: שהוא רק מצד השירה שאומרים,
phrases.en: that's because of this song that they're singing

phrases.he: בחינת הצורה ונפש הגלגל בהשתחוואה רוחנית כו'
phrases.en: their spiritual soul of the *galgal* is singing the praise, that causes the physical thing to always orbit

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר ודי למבין
phrases.en: as explained elsewhere, and that is enough to understand

blocks.text: The reason the planets revolve constantly is the song they sing. Their power comes from their bittul to G-d; deeper laws of reality create them, and they comply, which shows in their constant motion. Their spiritual soul sings the praise, which causes the physical thing always to orbit.
A simple person says they move because of gravity and the other laws of nature G-d created; the Rebbe called them the laws of creation.
Deeper still: why gravity has its value and the speed of light its value. These are set by the utterances of *Malchus*, G-d's speech, and the *malachim* are *batel* to them.
A way of *hisbonenus*: look all the way down to the physical world we are in, and see how everything we see is coming from G-d, as the Rambam talks about.

Everything is made of the four elements, and the stars and planets combine the fundamental forces that act on them. Changing gravity between the sun and the moon creates the tides; changing the sun's heat creates the weather, the evaporation of water, and the wind. Those are like the malachim of the Ofanim, and that creates everything.
All of it rests on the tuning of these laws and their underlying mathematics, the *Seraphim* of *Asiya*, and all of it is because G-d said so.

Physical things have spiritual properties. There is no reason they must be this way except that G-d wants it, and it is all for us to serve Hashem and do Torah and mitzvos, which is the world of *Beriya*.

Until we see the G-dliness in everything and the essence of Hashem, we should train ourselves, when looking at the world, to recognize G-d in all of it: it is easier in nature, but more covered up in man-made things.

Even a bridge works because G-d set up the laws; otherwise it would collapse. G-d gives us the ability to think and understand. So we should train ourselves to see G-d's hand, and the G-dliness, in everything.
